instruction: You are given the incomplete OpenFOAM template `/home/user/Desktop/heat_base/`. From the command line, build and solve a deterministic plate-conduction case. 1. Write `/home/user/Desktop/build_case.py` and create `/home/user/Desktop/heat/`. Build a two-dimensional rectangular plate `0<=x<=1.0 m`, `0<=y<=0.5 m`, with one `0.01 m` spanwise cell and `frontAndBack` empty. Use one uniform `200 x 20 x 1` block (4,000 cells). 2. Set the left wall to `400 K`, right wall to `300 K`, top and bottom walls adiabatic, initial internal temperature `350 K`, and thermal diffusivity `DT=0.01 m^2/s`. Configure `laplacianFoam` with implicit Euler, `deltaT=0.05 s`, `endTime=50 s`, and ASCII output only at 50 s. Source `/opt/openfoam11/etc/bashrc`, run `blockMesh -case /home/user/Desktop/heat` and retain `heat/log.blockMesh`, then run `laplacianFoam -case /home/user/Desktop/heat` and retain `heat/log.laplacianFoam`; both must finish with `End`, and time 50 must exist. Run `postProcess -case /home/user/Desktop/heat -latestTime -func writeCellCentres` and retain `heat/log.cellCentres`. 3. Write `/home/user/Desktop/postprocess.py`. Verify all 4,000 cell temperatures against the one-dimensional steady theory `T(x)=400-100*x K`; the whole-field RMS error must be at most `1 K`. Save the 200 points on the cell-center row nearest `y=0.25 m`, sorted by x, to `/home/user/Desktop/temperature_profile.csv` with `x_m,temperature_K,linear_theory_K`. 4. Select the cells nearest `(0.25,0.25) m` and `(0.75,0.25) m` (each x coordinate within 0.006 m), and save `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as exactly `temp_a, temp_b` in K. Do not use ParaView or other GUI tools. [Init Package Note] The uploaded template is an editable input only; no result or answer artifacts are preloaded. [Software] Source `/opt/openfoam11/etc/bashrc` before running OpenFOAM commands.
